subject: physics
title: Компас на корабле, пункт d
statement:
A ship can be thought of as a symmetric arrangement of soft iron. In the presence of an external magnetic field, the soft iron will become magnetized, creating a second, weaker magnetic field. We want to examine the effect of the ship's field on the ship's compass, which will be located in the middle of the ship. Let the strength of the Earth's magnetic field near the ship be $B_e$, and the orientation of the field be horizontal, pointing directly toward true north. The Earth's magnetic field $B_e$ will magnetize the ship, which will then create a second magnetic field $\vec{B}_s$ in the vicinity of the ship's compass given by $\vec{B}_s = B_e\left(-K_b\cos\theta\,\hat{b} + K_s\sin\theta\,\hat{s}\right)$ where $K_b$ and $K_s$ are positive constants, $\theta$ is the angle between the heading of the ship and magnetic north, measured clockwise, $\hat{b}$ and $\hat{s}$ are unit vectors pointing in the forward direction of the ship (bow) and directly right of the forward direction (starboard), respectively. Because of the ship's magnetic field, the ship's compass will no longer necessarily point North.

**Пункт d.** If the iron balls are placed directly to the right and left of the ship compass at distance $d$ chosen to cancel the error at the angles where $\delta\theta$ is largest, find the resulting expression for the combined deviation $\delta\theta$ due to the ship and the balls for all angles $\theta$.
